liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **KC Moan** (1 review): Listener calls it the first KC Moan, of interest to fans of the Dog [13]
- **This Time Forever** (1 review): Jerry's vocal on this song is singled out as sweet [13]
- **Deep Elem Blues** (1 review): Listener finds this performance heartbreaking [16]
- **Oh Boy** (1 other source): Source tape fades out during Jerry's closing talk rather than at the song's end [4]
- **Big Boy Pete** (1 other source): Soundboard is missing about 25 seconds in this song [5]

## The recordings

- **gd78-11-17.paud.wiley.11488.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 12 songs; 91 min; rated 3.09/5 by 11 [1]
- **gd78-11-17.acoustic.sbd.dodd.7687.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 44 min; rated 4.58/5 by 33 [3]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is very decent; the posted track list is wrong, though every song, KC Moan included, is present; Good sound, with the audience so audible that it feels like being in the room; Sounds like a small bar in Chicago, with good sound quality [11][12][15]
- **gd1978-11-17.sbd.dodd.audiohead22.remaster-7687.90110.sbefail.flac16**: soundboard; 10 songs; 45 min; rated 4.2/5 by 10 [4]
- **gd1978-11-17.acoustic.sbd.samaritano.32879.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 12 songs; 63 min; rated 3.86/5 by 7 [2]

## Around the show

- Acoustic set played for charity in a small venue to a small crowd [8]
- Band and audience interact closely, and the crowd responds eagerly to the set [8]
- Billed as a Bob Weir show, with Garcia sitting in throughout and Mickey Hart for most of it [11]
- Crowd sounds somewhat pushy, but Bob and Jerry shrug it off [12]
- Stage banter is memorable, including Jerry saying he is new around here [14]
- Acoustic Dead without Keith and Donna Godchaux; Mickey joined from Deep Elem Blues through the end [5]
- Dates from before the Dead played Heaven's Door [13]
- Offers a foretaste of the acoustic shows at Radio City, New Orleans and the Warfield two years later [18]
- Weir's guitar tone here is preferred to the harsher treble-heavy sound he gets elsewhere [19]
- Described as the only time the band played acoustically [5]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd78-11-17.paud.wiley.11488.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [1]
- **gd78-11-17.acoustic.sbd.dodd.7687.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Soundboard source passed along via Ernie Dodd, soundboard to unknown generations to shn [3]
- **gd1978-11-17.sbd.dodd.audiohead22.remaster-7687.90110.sbefail.flac16**: transferred by audiohead22; source: Soundboard [4]. Also: Remastered in 2008 by Audiohead22 in Cool Edit Pro: hiss reduced, EQ applied, reel glitches repaired, tracks re-split [4]
- **gd1978-11-17.acoustic.sbd.samaritano.32879.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Joe Samaritano; source: Soundboard->Master Cassette->DAT->Sonic Solutions->CD [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1978-11-17 Rambler Room, Loyola University, Chicago IL - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1978-11-17-rambler-room-loyola-university-chicago-il/) [21]
- Fan art by Jerry Garcia: [Rambler Room, Loyola College, Chicago, IL - 11/17/1978 - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/rambler-room-loyola-college-chicago-il-11-17-1978-17/) [22]
